OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '^.*\S.*$'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '^.*\S.*$'
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^\D*(\d\D*){10}$'
          example: '6085551023'
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            pets:
              title: Pets
              description: The pets owned by this individual including any booked vet visits.
              type: array
              items:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
              readOnly: true
          required:
            - pets
    OwnerPage:
      title: Owner page
      description: A page of pet owners.
      type: object
      properties:
        content:
          title: Content
          description: Pet owners in the requested page.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/Owner'
        page:
          title: Page
          description: Zero-based page index.
          type: integer

## Summary

I implemented the optional owner `email` rule as small, cohesive additions rather than by growing any existing method.

**What changed (behaviour lives in new, trivial units):**

1. **`openapi.yml`** — added an optional `email` property to the `OwnerFields` schema with `format: email`. Since the generator runs with `performBeanValidation`, the generated `OwnerFieldsDto` gets a `@Email` constraint, and the existing `@Valid` on the endpoint yields a **400** for a present-but-invalid address (`not-an-email`). It's absent from `required`, so a missing email is accepted. `email` also flows into the `Owner` response DTO via the `allOf`.

2. **`Owner.java`** — added an `email` field plus a fresh `getEmail`/`setEmail` pair (CC 1 each). `setEmail` lower-cases (mirroring the existing `setTelephone` normalization idiom), so it's **stored and returned lower-cased**. No existing method was touched, and MapStruct auto-maps `email` by name in both directions, so the mapper and controllers needed no edits.

3. **DB schemas** — added a nullable `email` column to all four `schema.sql` files (hsqldb/h2/mysql/postgres). The hsqldb `data.sql` seed used positional `INSERT INTO owners VALUES (...)`, so I gave those inserts an explicit column list (one `replace_all`) to stay valid with the new column.

**Verification** — the three new acceptance tests pass: mixed-case email stored/returned as `test.user@example.com`, invalid email → 400, missing email → 2xx. The log confirms the `@Email` violation is what produces the 400. No functions were modified in high-complexity classes (controllers/mappers untouched); the only edited Java unit is the small `Owner` accessor pair.
